record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.context_brief: Equations of state without chemical equilibrium
record.original_question: How can equations of state for hot and dense thermal matter be developed for both confined and deconfined conditions without assuming chemical equilibrium?

evidence.quote: Develop the equations of state of hot and dense thermal matter in confined and deconfined conditions without assumptions about chemical equilibrium.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Develop a theoretical framework for the equations of state of hot and dense thermal matter, valid in both the confined (hadronic) phase and the deconfined (quark–gluon) phase, without imposing chemical equilibrium among the particle species. Concretely: construct thermodynamic potentials (e.g., pressure P(T, {μ_i}, {n_i}), energy density ε, entropy density s) as functions of temperature T, conserved-charge chemical potentials, and the independent number densities n_i of each hadronic or partonic species (including strange and non-strange flavors), where the n_i are not constrained by detailed-balance chemical-equilibrium relations but evolve as independent variables. The framework should (i) reduce to the standard equilibrium equation of state when chemical equilibrium is imposed, (ii) preserve thermal (kinetic) equilibrium so that momentum distributions remain thermal at temperature T, (iii) be consistent with conservation of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness, and (iv) describe the transition between confined and deconfined regimes. Provide the explicit form of the pressure and the associated phase structure under these conditions.
artifact.category_tag: Equations of state in QCD thermodynamics
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad program-level open problem in finite-temperature QCD / heavy-ion phenomenology. Partial progress exists via off-equilibrium hadron resonance gas models, partial chemical equilibrium descriptions, and non-equilibrium parton/hadron transport (e.g., SMASH, PHSD), but no universally accepted formulation of an equation of state across confined and deconfined regimes without chemical-equilibrium assumptions has emerged. The status from web evidence is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Partial Chemical Equilibrium in Hadronic Matter
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses hadron gas thermodynamics with conserved abundances, an early formulation of off-equilibrium EoS.
status_evidence.claim: Partial chemical equilibrium frameworks exist but address only the hadronic side.

status_evidence.title: Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD)
status_evidence.snippet: Microscopic off-equilibrium transport across confined and deconfined regimes using a dynamical quasi-particle EoS.
status_evidence.claim: Non-equilibrium dynamical approaches model both phases but a closed-form non-equilibrium EoS remains an open development.
